newsitem.title: JAPAN: Need to watch if Japan surplus still declining - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Need to watch if Japan surplus still declining - MOF.

text.p: An official of Japan's Finance Ministry said on Wednesday that it is necessary to keep watch to see whether Japan's trade surplus remains on a declining trend.
"We need to continue to keep careful watch to see whether there has been a change in the declining trend of the trade surplus," the official told reporters.
He also said that the rise in Japan's consumption tax from April 1 was one of the special factors that had pushed up the trade surplus in April and May.

Asked about the future trend in the trade surplus with the United States, the official said that this would be affected by economic conditions in the United States and it was difficult to make predictions.

Asked whether weakness in the yen had been a factor in pushing up Japan's trade surplus in April and May, the official said: "This is one factor that affects trade but there are other factors like oil prices and economic conditions at home and abroad. I cannot say clearly that currencies were the only factor that affected trade."
He attributed the jump in May's trade surplus to a growth in exports exceeding that in imports.
Exports of cars and office equipment rose while imports of meat products dropped and this same trend was evident in trade with the United States, he said.

He added that although imports from the United States had continued to grow gradually, a drop in meat imports and an increase in exports of cars and office equipment had resulted in a rise in the surplus with that country.
